newsitem.title: UK: LME will seek membership approval on constitution.
newsitem.headline: LME will seek membership approval on constitution.

text.p: Any changes in the London Metal Exchange's (LME) governance structure after Thursday's SIB review will be fully discussed and put to the whole membership for approval, Exchange Chief Executive David King said.

One of the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) recommendations was that the LME review the composition of its Board to avoid potential conflicts of interest between regulatory duties and commercial interests. The LME was receptive to that, but it was a constitutional change that would need voting on, King added.

In coming weeks the Board would consider the issue and seek feedback to arrive at a common proposal that could be put to its members and have a clear passage, King said. "We would not propose anything against the wishes of the (whole) membership which comprises the ring-traders, associate broker-clearers, trade and associate members. That will be a democratic process," he said. The SIB suggested that the Board delegate responsibility for monitoring market trading and for intervention to maintain a proper market.

It also proposed that the LME review the make-up of its various committees and set up a Market Conduct Committee to oversee the setting and enforcement of trading and contract rules and regulations. The SIB, Britain's top regulator, carried out a wholesale review of the LME after the Sumitomo scandal in mid-June.
Sumitomo Corp of Japan fired its head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
